title: HOSA Nutrition: Medical Nutrition Therapy - Nutrition - Recall - Parenteral
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: What is the primary difference between Peripheral Parenteral Nutrition (PPN) and Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN)?
options: PPN uses the gut; TPN uses veins.
TPN has a higher dextrose concentration and requires a central line; PPN is more dilute.
PPN is for long-term use; TPN is for short-term.
questions.explain: TPN (Total Parenteral Nutrition) is hypertonic (high dextrose/osmolarity) and requires a large central vein. PPN (Peripheral) has lower osmolarity to prevent damaging smaller peripheral veins.
